item.title: Storm Austen Knocks Out Power to Nearly 300,000 French Homes
item.description: Austen is the first named storm this autumn and it’s also sending power prices in France and Germany tumbling. Storm Austen knocked out electricity to almost 300,000 customers in western France on Friday as hurricane-force winds battered the region, disrupting roads, railways and other transport links. Brittany was hardest hit, with almost 150,000 customers without power, according to distributor Enedis.

item.title: Insurance AI’s Next Test: Can Carriers Trust the Data?
item.description: Insurance companies are beginning to look toward the next phase of AI adoption with agentic AI and automation, according to Chris Newman, CEO of ACORD Solutions Group, at this year’s InsurTech Connect conference in Las Vegas. However, as AI moves further into insurance decision-making and business operations, insurers need confidence in the data supporting the technology. “But the challenge comes with the trust element in terms of can you trust your data.” This means questions of where the information originated, whether sources are verified, and if a carrier can account for how decisions are made, he said.

item.title: U.S. Announces $25M Whistleblower Program to Encourage Public to Report Alleged Fraud
item.description: President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance on Tuesday announced a $25 million program to encourage the public to blow the whistle on suspected fraud in the U.S. The White House said that under the Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program, anyone who submits a tip that leads to a fraud conviction or a significant federal enforcement action is eligible to receive up to $30,000, and that the Justice Department will administer the program. During the announcement, Trump said payments will amount to a 1% commission on the amount of fraud the tip helps uncover.

item.title: China’s Natural Disaster Losses Hit $30B in First Nine Months of 2026
item.description: China recorded 199.36 billion yuan ($29.9 billion) in direct losses from natural disasters in the first nine months of 2026, mainly driven by severe typhoons, flooding and landslides, its Ministry of Emergency Management said on Thursday. Overall, 1,162 people have died or have been classified as missing from China’s natural disasters in the first nine months of the year, up from 742 a year earlier. The losses were down 8% from 217.65 billion yuan over the same period last year.

item.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Robot Training, Space Lasers And Greener Cement
item.description: From teaching robots to do everyday household chores to using lasers to track satellites in space, this month’s crop of interesting startup deals spans some decidedly different corners of tech. This is a monthly column that runs down five interesting startup funding deals that may have flown under the radar. The startup says it has already captured more than 2 million hours of human activity, with 1.5 million hours ready for use in AI training.

item.title: Protecting Trade Secrets In The Age Of AI
item.description: That is exactly what the defendant attempted in a recent federal trade secrets case I litigated on behalf of a client in the U.S. Instead, he used stolen trade secrets as training inputs to build, essentially, an AI version of his old boss , attempting a shortcut to create a competing business without spending years developing the skills and expertise typically needed to provide such services. AI is creating new ways to misappropriate trade secrets, well beyond the classic theft story of an employee downloading files onto a thumb drive.

item.title: Fronting companies to engage more frequently with ILS market: AM Best
item.description: Rating agency AM Best has indicated in a new report that fronting companies are expected to engage more frequently with the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market to drive capacity diversification using catastrophe bonds, sidecars and collateralized reinsurance structures. The agency further noted that capacity diversification is likely to persist, as fronting companies are expected to engage with the insurance-linked securities market on a more frequent basis. In its report, AM Best notes that the property and casualty fronting market continued to grow at a healthy rate during 2025, driven in part by the sustained expansion of MGA-oriented business.

item.title: Munich Re raises full-year 2026 profit target as Q3 result well-above consensus
item.description: As a result, with this above the previous target that was expected, Munich Re has now raised its full-year 2026 profit target by €300 million, from €6.3 billion to €6.6 billion. Demonstrating the continued profitability of reinsurance underwriting businesses in 2026, global giant Munich Re has preliminarily reported its third-quarter net profit will be higher than consensus at €1.7 billion, on which basis the company has raised its full-year profit guidance by €300 million. Munich Re said today that the third-quarter of 2026 saw strong financial performance for the company, resulting in a net profit projected to be €1.7 billion, much higher than the analyst consensus estimate of €1.479 billion.

item.title: Catastrophe bond market to hit second $20bn+ issuance year at fastest pace yet
item.description: As the catastrophe bond market pipeline builds for the fourth-quarter of 2026, we are already tracking what will be only the second ever year where issuance of 144A catastrophe bonds and private cat bond deals has exceeded the $20 billion level, while currently the market remains on a faster issuance pace than 2025. Catastrophe bond market participants had entered 2026 with a view that the $20 billion of issuance milestone would be seen again this year. Following on from the landmark record year of cat bond issuance in 2025, when we tracked over $25.6 billion of issuance, across full Rule 144A and private cat bond deals ( see our quarterly cat bond market reports for all the details ), the expectation has always been that the market would continue to see a $20 billion plus level of issuance.

item.title: FM to provide 10% premium offset against eligible policies for the second year running
item.description: FM, a commercial property insurer focused on property protection, engineering and loss prevention, will provide eligible clients with an estimated $855 million through its resilience credit program, marking the second consecutive year that the firm is providing a 10% premium offset. The premium offset will be applied against eligible FM policies with renewals or anniversaries between January 1, 2027 and December 31, 2027. Up from 5% in 2024 and prior years, the 10% premium offset to eligible FM clients follows extraordinary results and historically low losses.

item.title: Neptune revenue hit record $59.6m in Q3’26
item.description: Florida-based flood insurance group, Neptune Insurance Holdings Inc., the parent of Neptune Flood, reported a 34.3%, or $15.2 million year-on-year increase in revenue to a record $59.6 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $44.4 million in the comparable prior year quarter. Revenues were driven by continued growth of the renewal portfolio, increased commission income, record new business sales, increased Neptune adoption by agents, and additional new business sales resulting from the Palomar agreement . For this quarter, Neptune’s written premiums grew by 31% to a record $132.7 million, and grew by more than 32% to $446.2 million over the last 12 months.

item.title: Everspan to sell its redundant admitted shell company to Falvey Insurance
item.description: Everspan Group, a specialty property and casualty insurance platform, has entered into a definitive agreement to sell Providence Washington Insurance Company (PWIC) to Rhode Island-based Falvey Insurance Group. The divestment of the admitted shell company is part of the company’s broader initiative to streamline operations and reduce overhead. Domiciled in Rhode Island, it was acquired by Everspan in 2021, becoming one of five P&C companies owned by the insurance platform.

item.title: Phoenix Hit by Hail and Strong Winds, Damaging Vehicles Across Valley
item.description: A severe storm on Wednesday produced hail the size of golf balls in metro Phoenix, damaging cars windshields across the Valley. North Phoenix, Glendale, Tempe and Mesa were among the Valley communities that felt the worst of the hail. While hailstorms are infrequent in Phoenix, the metro has experienced multiple severe storms in the past year, including a November 2025 storm that produced hail in the West Valley.

item.title: AM Best Revises Outlook to Stable for Ohio Mutual Insurance Group’s Members
item.description: AM Best has revised the outlook to stable from negative for the Long-Term Issuer Credit Ratings (Long-Term ICR) and affirmed the Financial Strength Rating (FSR) of A (Excellent) and the Long-Term ICRs of “a+” (Excellent) for the members of Ohio Mutual Insurance Group (OMIG) based in Bucyrus. The revision of the Long-Term ICR outlook to stable from negative reflects the improvement in OMIG’s operating performance resulting from management initiatives implemented over the past few years. The ratings reflect OMIG’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as strongest, as well as its strong operating performance, neutral business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management.

item.description: Zurich American does not get to reclassify a loss as one with a much higher deductible after it had already paid part of the claim, a federal appeals court said in a case involving rain damage to a massive solar farm in Georgia. District Court in the Middle District of Georgia found in favor of First Solar, the judge awarded $12.2 million, including prejudgment interest. 11 th Circuit Court of Appeals wrote in its Oct.

item.title: Munich Re raises 2026 profit guidance to €6.6bn on strong preliminary Q3 results
item.description: Munich Re has reported a preliminary net profit of approximately €1.7bn for the third quarter of 2026, driven by a “very pleasing” operating performance across all business segments, below-average major-loss expenditure in P&C reinsurance, and a strong investment result in reinsurance. With a preliminary net result of €5.7bn for the first nine months of 2026, Munich Re is now raising its full-year net profit guidance from €6.3bn to €6.6bn. The firm described the results as another quarter of strong financial performance, with its preliminary net profit comfortably exceeding the analyst consensus estimate of €1.479bn.

item.title: AIA appoints Edward Moncreiffe as Regional Chief Executive
item.description: AIA Group has announced the appointment of Edward Moncreiffe as regional chief executive, with effect from 2 November 2026. Prior to joining AIA, Moncreiffe was chief executive officer, insurance at HSBC Group, overseeing the life and health insurance business in Hong Kong, Macau, the Chinese Mainland, Singapore, India, Malta, Bermuda, and Mexico, as well as insurance distribution units globally. Lee Yuan Siong, AIA group chief executive and president, said Moncreiffe brought deep expertise and international experience.

item.title: Kin enables WebMCP for AI insurance shopping
item.description: Kin has enabled WebMCP in its online home insurance quoting process, allowing AI agents to interact with its website on consumers’ behalf. According to Kin, the integration lets consumers use ChatGPT to obtain a customized home insurance quote ready for purchase. WebMCP allows AI agents to interact directly with the website without installing a separate plug-in.

item.title: Asshield adds ChatGPT insurance quote requests
item.description: Independent agency Asshield Insurance has a ChatGPT app that collects insurance quote requests and routes them to licensed agents for follow-up. The app supports personal, commercial and recreational insurance, including auto, homeowners, renters, general liability, workers’ compensation, trucking, boat and golf cart coverage. Asshield says a licensed agent typically responds within about an hour during business hours.

item.title: Sure offers renters insurance quotes through ChatGPT
item.description: Sure has a ChatGPT app that lets users obtain renters insurance quotes through a guided conversation, with purchases completed on Sure’s website. The app, listed as Sure Renters Insurance, checks state availability and collects information about the applicant and rental property. The app brings information collection, coverage selection and quote creation into ChatGPT, giving Sure another channel to reach renters.

item.title: Control del coste médico en salud: el reto no es detectar más, sino actuar mejor
item.description: Ofrecer al asegurado una atención de calidad, ágil y sostenible exige aprovechar mejor los recursos destinados a su salud. Reducir el coste evitable por fraude, abusos, errores de facturación e ineficiencias ayuda a preservar esos recursos.

item.title: Cesiones de crédito: INESE analiza el 28 de octubre los retos jurídicos y operativos
item.description: La cesión de créditos se ha convertido en una herramienta habitual en la gestión de siniestros de automóvil. Centros sanitarios, talleres y, más recientemente, empresas intermediarias entre lesionados y prestadores médicos recurren a ella para sustituir al perjudicado original y reclamar directamente a las aseguradoras el coste de los servicios prestados a las víctimas de accidentes de tráfico, o incluso la indemnización que corresponde al propio asegurado según su póliza.

item.title: AI Safety Group METR Finds Flaws in OpenAI’s Internal Monitoring System
item.description: AI safety research group METR said on Thursday a pilot exercise to stress-test OpenAI’s internal monitoring system uncovered several new vulnerabilities, including an exploit that AI agents could have used to keep hundreds of their recent actions from being monitored. The researchers found a way OpenAI’s Codex coding agents could, in principle, bypass safety restrictions and take any action available to the user running them, as well as two settings that could switch off monitoring for new agents. Only about 75% to 94% of OpenAI’s internal AI agent traffic from models at least as powerful as GPT-5.5 was eligible for monitoring, the researchers estimated.

item.title: Washington Updates Insurance Claims Handling Rules, Deadlines
item.description: New claims handling rules in Washington require insurers to follow updated rules that establish deadlines for responding to policyholders, conducting investigations, issuing denials and making payments. The updated rules issued by Washington Insurance Commissioner Patty Kuderer revise standards for handling claims that had not been updated since their adoption in 1978. 18, require insurers to notify policyholders within 30 days whether claims have been accepted or denied and provide updates every 30 days if a claim is delayed.

item.title: FCA restricts 6 firms following concerns over anti-money laundering controls
item.description: Restrictions have been placed on 6 unregulated lenders, known as Annex 1 firms, after the FCA raised concerns about their anti-money laundering policies, controls and procedures while assessing their applications. These firms operate in sectors that can present a heightened risk of money laundering and other financial crime and are required to register with the FCA for supervision under the Money Laundering Regulations. Registration under the Money Laundering Regulations is not a substitute for regulated firms carrying out their own appropriate due diligence.

item.title: FCA calls on private market firms to manage conflicts of interest in line with rapid growth
item.description: Private market firms vary in how well they identify and manage conflicts of interest, according to an FCA review. Michelle Beck, director of wholesale buy-side at the FCA, said: 'Firms need to ensure their management of conflicts of interest keeps pace with growth in their size and complexity. As private markets grow and business models become more complex, the FCA found that some firms were failing to identify conflicts adequately or keep their controls up to date.

item.title: Insurance-linked securities attract DACH investor interest, allocations to rise: BAI survey
item.description: There are a number of interesting data points relevant to catastrophe bonds and insurance-linked securities as an alternative asset class, most important of which are the rising investor allocations to and interest in ILS assets. A survey of 105 institutional investors across the DACH-region undertaken by the German association for alternative investments, shows that an increasing number of allocators in the region are choosing catastrophe bonds and insurance-linked securities, while more indicate they intend to enter the sector. The organisations annual survey highlights why institutional investors in the DACH-region (Germany, Austria, and Switzerland) invest in private markets and alternative strategies, as well as where there focus will be in the future.

item.title: Bishop Street names Fiato Chief Business Officer, Wilson appointed CEO of CIS and President of AIM
item.description: As Chief Business Officer, he will extend that experience across our broader platform, helping our companies navigate growth while allowing their teams to focus on underwriting and serving their partners.” “I am grateful for the opportunity to take on this expanded role at Bishop Street,” said Fiato. Bill Wilson will be succeeding Fiato as Chief Executive Officer of Conifer Insurance Services, LLC (CIS) and President of Aerospace Insurance Managers (AIM). Following Bishop Street’s acquisition of CIS in 2024, he served as Senior Vice President, Corporate Counsel and Secretary of CIS before being named President in 2025 and Chief Executive Officer in 2026.

item.title: Donegal expands partnership with ZestyAI, adding Z-PROPERTY
item.description: Donegal Insurance Group has expanded its partnership with ZestyAI, a provider of AI-driven insurance risk analytics, adding Z-PROPERTY™ to deepen its understanding of the properties and exposures across its personal lines portfolio. This builds on their existing partnership, which began in 2025, when Donegal selected ZestyAI’s Roof Age solution to improve its internal data and understanding of property risk across its homeowners business. With Z-PROPERTY, Donegal is bringing that same accuracy and verification to critical property variables, including roof condition, roof complexity, lot debris and other features that affect risk and premium.

item.title: Pinion names Robert Carlaw as Chief Technical Officer to advance Sarrus platform development
item.description: Pinion Insurance, a London-based specialty insurance carrier established in 2026, has appointed Robert Carlaw as Chief Technical Officer (CTO). Philip Vandoninck, Co-Founder and Group Chief Underwriting Officer at Pinion, added: “Robert brings a rare combination of deep technical expertise, leadership experience and a proven track record of delivering technology that supports real business outcomes. Attracting senior talent from more technology-advanced industries is an important part of bringing new thinking into insurance and accelerating the pace of innovation across the sector.” Carlaw will be responsible for directing the ongoing development of Sarrus as Pinion grows its specialty insurance business.

item.title: Viewpoint: Generational Shifts, Delayed Projects Are Shaping Builder’s Risk
item.description: Having spent more than 20 years in the industry, including a decade focusing on builder’s risk, I have seen the market shift numerous times over the years. In my opinion, here’s what lies behind the three biggest factors currently influencing Builder’s Risk: The number of submissions for Builder’s Risk are up compared to recent years, but the time from quote to bind is considerably longer. Builder’s Risk claims always occur many months after policy inception and project delays are stretching timelines out even further.

item.title: AM Best: Social Inflation Drives Surge in Commercial Auto Liability Claims
item.description: Historically, umbrella pricing followed closely with general liability but more recently, David Blades, associate director at AM Best said, “As social inflation began to impact commercial auto claims, and those claims spilled into the umbrella coverage, umbrella pricing diverged from general liability, becoming more costly.” Topics Auto Claims Commercial Lines Business Insurance AM Best Liability AM Best Special Report: Social Inflation Adds Pressure to US Property/Casualty Liability Results Commercial auto liability losses are capped by policy limits, typically $1 million. However, as social inflation began to impact commercial auto claims, and those claims spilled into umbrella coverages, the pricing on the latter has diverged from general liability, becoming more costly, and has yet to return to its prior level.

item.description: Apollo Underwriting , a Skyward Group company, has partnered with Generali to launch Red Bridge Syndicate 2031 at Lloyd’s. Red Bridge will allow Lloyd’s members to participate in Generali’s outward reinsurance program, which covers multiple lines of business across Europe. The launch will bring Apollo’s total number of syndicates under management to 11, expanding its third-party syndicate management business and generating additional fee-based revenue for Skyward Group.

item.title: Donegal Expands ZestyAI Property Risk Capabilities
item.description: “The carriers pulling ahead are the ones whose decisions rest on data they can defend.” ZestyAI says it has received more than 500 regulatory approvals nationwide for its property-risk models and related capabilities. (Image source: IIR.) Donegal Insurance Group (Marietta, Pa.) has expanded its relationship with ZestyAI (San Francisco), adding the vendor’s Z-PROPERTY solution to support property-level underwriting and portfolio decisions across its personal lines business. With Z-PROPERTY, Donegal is extending that approach to additional property characteristics including roof condition, roof complexity, lot debris and other features that can affect risk and premium.

item.title: Cotality Launches Supplement Claims Workflow Portal
item.description: “Cotality Supplement solves this conflict with a single, transparent workflow.” Looking Beyond Individual Supplements Cotality says the portal also provides analytics around supplement volume, costs and recurring causes, giving claims leaders greater visibility into patterns that may be driving repeated requests. (Image source: IIR.) Cotality (Irvine, Calif.) has launched Cotality Supplement , a configurable white-label portal designed to streamline property claims supplement workflows between carriers and contractors. Cotality Supplement automatically routes requests to the appropriate claims team and generates side-by-side variance reports showing changes between original and supplemental estimates, including additions, removals and pricing differences.

Malibu Life , through its insurance subsidiary TruSpire Retirement Insurance Company (Irving, Texas), and Legacy Marketing Group (Petaluma, Calif.) have announced the launch of PillarMark with MultiRider and SpireMark with MultiRider Max, two fixed indexed annuities designed to address different retirement income needs. The products mark the launch of Malibu’s U.S. “Retirement looks different for every individual, and we believe the products we bring to market should reflect that,” comments Todd Shriber, CEO, Malibu Life.

item.title: World Food Programme buys parametric tropical cyclone insurance from CCRIF
item.description: CCRIF SPC, the regional parametric risk pool for the Caribbean and Central America, has announced that the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) has become the first UN agency and multilateral organisation to join and purchase parametric insurance from it. WFP has purchased two parametric tropical cyclone policies to cover the Dominican Republic and Haiti from CCRIF, with the insurance having a combined coverage limit of US $11.6 million. The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) has been utilising parametric risk transfer as a way to secure disaster contingent financing to support its operations for nearing two decades.

item.title: Moody’s establishes casualty risk intelligence group with six founding organisations
item.description: Moody’s, a global provider of financial data, risk analysis and business intelligence, has established the Moody’s Casualty Risk Intelligence Group (MCRIG), an initiative involving six founding organisations from across the insurance industry. We are proud to launch the MCRIG in New York and to do so with such a strong and diverse group of founding participants.” Noel Richardson, Chief Risk Officer at AXA XL, added: “Casualty insurance faces significant complexity from emerging risks such as PFAS and AI liability, yet the industry relies largely on backward-looking analysis. Joe Melly, Managing Director and Head of Casualty and Financial Lines at Moody’s, commented: “Casualty insurance is the next frontier for risk analytics, and Moody’s is committed to leading that transformation.

item.title: Renew Risk expands solar farm catastrophe modelling to all 48 contiguous US states
item.description: Renew Risk, a specialist provider of risk analytics for renewable energy and energy demand assets, has expanded its severe convective storm (SCS) modelling capabilities for solar farms to cover all 48 contiguous US states. As the industry expands, Renew Risk is adapting its modelling to reflect changes in the size, location and technical design of solar installations. Renew Risk’s expanded model enables insurers, reinsurers and brokers to assess three key severe convective storm hazards across the contiguous United States.

item.title: W.R. Berkley projects reinsurance contraction of up to 20% amid ‘challenging’ market conditions
item.description: Berkley Corporation is bracing for a continued pullback in its assumed reinsurance operations, warning that deteriorating market conditions across both casualty and property lines will likely drive a double-digit contraction in segment volume over the foreseeable future. He said: “I guess there’s no point in crying any further over spilt milk, but when the day’s all done, as you have heard us talk about for several quarters now, there’s a dissatisfaction with market conditions within casualty, reinsurance, and property. As the reinsurance market remains competitive, Berkley is keen on maintaining underwriting discipline, which is reflected in the segment’s net premiums written declining 11.6% to $369 million, driven by casualty and, to a lesser extent, property.
